sources.title: bb README.md
sources.finding: bb has desktop/browser/CLI/API surfaces, uses authenticated provider CLIs, supports macOS arm64 desktop and alpha Linux/Windows clients. Production telemetry is on and BB_TELEMETRY=false disables it. Electron shell is documented.

sources.title: bb packages/bb-app/README.md
sources.finding: The npm package bundles launcher, bb CLI and Node SDK. It uses installed Claude Code, Codex, Pi or ACP providers and existing logins; server and daemon have separate restart/logging behavior.

sources.title: bb docs/system-overview.md
sources.finding: Server owns SQLite state, HTTP/WebSocket API and host routing. Enrolled daemons execute work. Manager threads coordinate child threads, with append-only events and explicit lifecycle relationships.

sources.title: bb docs/multiple-devices.md
sources.finding: An always-on desktop/server/VM runs bb while remote browsers/phones steer threads. Additional host daemons execute work. bb connect is account-gated; direct API access relies on a trusted network and is unauthenticated.

sources.title: bb docs/platform-support.md
sources.finding: iOS TestFlight and Android APK clients connect to the server. Phone apps are control clients with documented surface limitations, not execution hosts.

sources.title: bb docs/worktrees.md
sources.finding: Managed worktrees create separate branches, copy selected untracked files and run setup/teardown hooks. Setup failures prevent thread start; this is file separation, not a claimed security sandbox.

sources.title: bb plugins/tasks/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Tasks plugin has persistent IDs, list/board views, labels, priorities, subtasks, comments, attachments and explicit delegation into worker threads. bb tasks CLI reads/writes the same tracker and reports results.

sources.title: bb plugins/automations/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Automations run cron/timezone or one-shot schedules, create/re-prompt threads or run stored scripts, and retain run output/history. Scheduler scripts execute on the server host.

sources.title: bb plugins/concurrency-limit/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Automatic host capacity is one running thread per processor, with host/global overrides. New turns wait at capacity and reconsider when running threads settle.

sources.title: bb plugins/memory/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Memory plugin stores global/project records with provenance, versions, edit/delete UI and version-checked CLI writes. Summary catalog is injected each turn.

sources.title: bb plugins/mcp/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Local/remote MCP exposes bb CLI search/read/run; remote apps require account approval and can be revoked. Write access is all-or-nothing and can steer agents on controlled hosts.

sources.title: bb plugins/provider-claude-code/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Claude provider runs the installed signed-in Claude CLI and reads plan/usage; permission modes and optional disabling of provider-native subagents are documented.

sources.title: bb plugins/provider-codex/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: Codex supports ChatGPT login or API key, shows ChatGPT usage limits and can disable provider-native subagents so delegation uses bb.

sources.title: bb docs/configuration.md
sources.finding: Git change summaries, optional commit action, PR status/readiness/merge actions and disabled-by-default retention policies are configurable. Interrupted-thread resume is experimental and off by default.

sources.title: bb plugins/git/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: The Git plugin displays uncommitted, branch and per-commit diffs, Viewed marks and filters, with CLI operations against the same environment.

sources.title: bb CHANGELOG.md
sources.finding: Current source changelog describes stuck-turn timeouts, provider retry de-duplication and reconnect catch-up. Automatic interrupted-thread resumption remains opt-in.

sources.title: bb LICENSE
sources.finding: The application repository is MIT licensed.

sources.title: bb plugins/environment-modal-sandbox/README.md
sources.locator: Standard image; Settings and commands; configuration.ts account token requirements; shipped environment plugin directory and provider implementations
sources.finding: The optional official Modal sandbox plugin builds a named Dockerfile image, creates a reusable sandbox machine in the user Modal account, enrolls its daemon and clones projects. Operator Modal credentials pay provider infrastructure; bb supplies no vendor-operated execution service. The shipped environment backend set has host checkout/worktree or Modal image-based sandbox, with no selectable VM/microVM backend.

sources.title: bb docs/multiple-devices.md
sources.locator: Browser device and Open bb from another browser; apps/server/src/routes/threads/actions.ts; browser-request-guard.ts; core/account authentication and permission models inspected
sources.finding: A bb server can be opened by multiple browser devices to send prompts and manage the same threads. Direct trusted-network API access has no per-human authentication; bb connect gates the tunnel to its paired account owner. Core thread actions accept shared thread input/queued follow-ups, without a human organization-role model or enterprise SSO integration.

sources.title: bb plugins/provider-codex/PLUGIN_OVERVIEW.md
sources.finding: The official Codex provider uses the operator codex login on the execution machine and explicitly accepts a ChatGPT account or OpenAI API key. bb remains a free MIT application; those model charges are paid through the provider account, not a bb plan.
